title: Pocket calculator
hints: Split the job in two: first a tokenizer that turns the string into `Token[]` (numbers and operators, spaces skipped, anything else throws), then an evaluator over the tokens.

Precedence trick without a full parser: do one pass that collapses `*` and `/` into a list of terms, then a second pass that sums the terms with `+`/`-`, left to right. (Or: a tiny recursive-descent parser with `parseExpr` → `parseTerm`.)

Evaluator sketch: `let terms = [first number]; let ops = []` — for each (op, num): if op is `*` or `/`, replace the last term with `last op num`; else push op and num. Finally fold `terms` left-to-right with `ops`. Check that tokens alternate number/operator, else throw.
